questions.q: A family consisting of a father, a mother, and seven children is best described as a:
options: Small family size
Large family size
Extended family size
Modern family size
questions.explain: According to the syllabus, a **large family size** is characterized by the presence of a father, mother, and **many children**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.topic: The Consequences of Large and Small Family Sizes

questions.q: Which of the following characteristics best describes a small family size?
options: A father, mother, and very few children
A father, three mothers, and their relatives
A mother, grandmother, and ten children
A father, mother, and many children
questions.explain: A **small family size** is identified primarily by having a father, mother, and **very few children** (e.g., one to three children).
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.topic: The Consequences of Large and Small Family Sizes

questions.q: How does a small family size generally affect the quality of an individual child's life compared to a large family size?
options: The child receives less parental attention and affection
The child is more likely to drop out of school due to high sibling competition
The child often enjoys better health, nutrition, and qualitative education
The child is forced to engage in child labour earlier in life
questions.explain: Because resources are shared among fewer people, children in a small family generally experience a higher quality of life, including **better nutrition, parental attention, and qualitative education**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.topic: The Consequences of Large and Small Family Sizes

questions.q: What is a likely consequence of a very large family size on the family's economic resources?
options: Resources become extremely abundant for each child
Financial resources are strained, often leading to poverty
The parents automatically receive larger salaries from employers
The family effortlessly saves more money in the bank
questions.explain: In a large family, financial and material resources are stretched thin to cater to many children, which heavily **strains the family's budget and can lead to poverty**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.topic: The Consequences of Large and Small Family Sizes

questions.q: On a national level, a widespread culture of maintaining very large family sizes is likely to result in which of the following for the economy?
options: Decreased demand for imported goods
Excessive pressure on public infrastructure and high unemployment
Automatic increase in the country's foreign financial reserves
A reduction in the nation's crime rate
questions.explain: When the population grows rapidly due to large family sizes, it creates **excessive pressure on the national economy**, overwhelming public amenities like schools and hospitals, and resulting in higher unemployment.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.topic: The Consequences of Large and Small Family Sizes

questions.q: Which type of family size is most favorable for rapid national economic savings and infrastructural development?
options: Small family size
Large family size
Uncontrolled family size
Polygamous large family size
questions.explain: A **small family size** contributes to a manageable national population growth rate, allowing the government to effectively plan, provide adequate infrastructure, and grow the national economy.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.topic: The Consequences of Large and Small Family Sizes

questions.q: One of the negative consequences of a large family size on maternal health is:
options: Increased lifespan of the mother
Deterioration of the mother's health due to frequent childbearing
Better physical fitness from doing more household chores
Complete immunity from genetic diseases
questions.explain: Frequent and numerous pregnancies required to produce a large family can take a severe toll on the physical health of the mother, causing **deterioration and high maternal health risks**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.topic: The Consequences of Large and Small Family Sizes

questions.q: Why do parents in a small family generally find it easier to provide high-quality education for their children?
options: Schools charge lower fees for small families
They have less money to spend on luxuries
The financial burden is limited to only a few children
Children from small families are naturally smarter
questions.explain: Because the **financial resources are concentrated on very few children**, the parents can afford higher-quality schooling and educational materials without excessive strain.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.topic: The Consequences of Large and Small Family Sizes

questions.q: High dependency ratio in a nation's economy is strongly linked to:
options: A high number of small families
An increase in large family sizes producing numerous non-working dependents
A widespread practice of celibacy among youths
An increase in factory construction
questions.explain: Large families produce many children who are dependents (they consume but do not produce economically yet), thereby increasing the nation's **dependency ratio**.
questions.exam: BECE National Values Education: Social Studies
questions.subject: National Values Education
questions.topic: The Consequences of Large and Small Family Sizes

questions.q: Overcrowding in a residential home is a direct characteristic consequence of:
options: A small family living in an estate
A large family size living in limited housing space
Single parenting
Delaying childbearing
questions.explain: Because there are many members in a **large family**, they often experience **overcrowding** and lack of personal space if the family cannot afford a massive house.
